Build on Fedimint Card

The card holds spend keys and a PIN. A till builds each Fedimint transaction, the card signs its hash, and a registry records which notes belong to which card. This page covers the parts, the card's commands and how to test them.

How the parts fit

  • The card. A Java Card applet on an NXP J3R180 chip. It makes BIP340 keys in 8 slots, guards signing with a PIN and signs a 32-byte hash. It never sees a transaction or an amount, and no command returns a private key.
  • The till. card-sidecar, a Rust service built on the Fedimint client. It joins a federation, plans which notes to spend, builds the transaction, collects the card's signatures and submits it. The till's own wallet receives the merchant's ecash.
  • The POS phone. An Android or iOS app that reads the card over NFC, takes the PIN and passes card commands to the till.
  • The registry. A Cloudflare Worker at registry.fedimintcard.org that records each card's notes by its short id, the last 4 bytes of its slot-0 public key. Tills read and update it on every payment. See Privacy for what it can see.
  • The provisioner. The operator's phone app. It installs the applet over NFC, sets each card's management keys and PIN, and approves new tills.
  • The federation. A Fedimint federation running the mintv2 module. Its guardians check each note's signature and mark it spent.

Status

Fedimint Card is an experimental prototype. The applet and till have been tested on NXP J3R180 cards with a few phones, and have had no outside security review. A card holds at most 8 notes, so many prices leave change it cannot hold and the till refuses them. Cards with 32 slots are in development.

Build against it to learn and give feedback. Read the risks before anyone holds real value on a card.

The card's commands

AID F0464D4341524401, class byte B0. Slots are numbered 0 to 7 in P1, and P2 is 0 unless noted.

INSCommandDataAnswer
10GEN_KEYnone. P2 = 1 replaces a used slot32-byte x-only public key
11GET_PUBnone32-byte x-only public key
12SIGN32-byte message64-byte BIP340 signature
40VERIFY_PINPIN, 4 to 8 bytesopens a signing session
41SET_PINPIN, 4 to 8 bytesonce per card
42CHANGE_PINold PIN then new PIN, same lengthneeds VERIFY_PIN; ends the session
  • A verified PIN lasts for one selection. Any SELECT or card reset ends it, so VERIFY_PIN and SIGN must happen in the same selection.
  • Three wrong PINs block the card for good. There is no unblock command.
  • SIGN checks the PIN before the slot, so a reader without the PIN cannot learn which slots hold keys.
  • Signatures use fresh randomness, so the same message signed twice gives different signatures.
  • On a J3R180, SIGN takes about 850 ms, GEN_KEY about 125 ms and GET_PUB about 27 ms.
Status wordMeaning
9000Done
63CXWrong PIN, X tries left
6983PIN blocked
6984No PIN set
6A94PIN set but not verified in this selection
6985Refused in this state: slot used or empty, or a PIN already set
6700 6B00Wrong length; bad P1 or P2
6D00 6E00Unknown INS; wrong class byte
6F00Crypto failure

How a payment is built

  • Each note on the card is a Fedimint mintv2 note whose nonce is one slot's public key. Note amounts are powers of two in msat.
  • The till plans the inputs, the merchant's output and the card's change, balanced to the exact msat. Change goes to fresh keys in free slots.
  • The till builds the transaction with NaiveMultisig. The card signs the 32-byte tx_hash, which covers every input and output, once for each note spent.
  • Before signing, the till records its intent with the registry. After the federation decides, it records the outcome and the card's new notes.

The till API

The till listens on 127.0.0.1:9877 by default. Any other address needs a POS token, made by card-sidecar till pair and sent as Authorization: Bearer.

  • POST /v1/charge takes price_msat, an optional client_ref and the PIN. It usually answers in 5 to 20 seconds. A repeated client_ref never spends twice.
  • POST /v1/card/balance, GET /v1/sales, GET /v1/status and GET /v1/health.
  • POST /v1/cards/precheck, /v1/cards/keySetup and /v1/cards/issue set up and load a card.
  • GET /v1/card/link is the WebSocket a POS phone uses to pass card commands to the till.
  • Errors answer {"ok":false,"error","detail"}. Among them: wrong_pin, pin_blocked, insufficient, no_exact_plan (the card cannot hold the change), undecided (the federation has not answered yet) and card_changed.

The till API reference has every field and error, and POS link covers the phone's side.

The registry

  • Operators sign in with a password for a 12-hour token. Operator accounts are made only through a deploy secret, never over HTTP.
  • Tills get their own revocable tokens. A till asks for one with a claim code, and an operator approves it in the provisioner (till claim).
  • A till or operator sees only its own operator's cards. Any other card answers 404.
  • Each card's management keys are derived from a registry secret and kept there, so only its operator can reinstall or reset it.

The operations plan covers the design and the decisions behind it.

The code

Everything is in fedimintcard/fedimintcard.

  • applet/: the Java Card applet, with jCardSim tests.
  • bridge/: the real applet in jCardSim behind a small HTTP API on 127.0.0.1.
  • host/: Rust. The card crate talks to a card through a software card, the bridge or PC/SC; sidecar is the till and its command line; fed-tests runs a 4-guardian federation inside cargo test.
  • registry/: the registry Worker, in TypeScript on a Durable Object.
  • apps/provisioner/: the operator app, React Native for Android and iOS.
  • tools/cardkit/: the GlobalPlatform engine that installs and resets the applet, shared with Cashu Card.
  • android-relay/ and ios-pos/: the POS apps.

The design note explains why the card works as it does, and the spike results hold the first measurements on silicon.

Testing without a card

# the applet in jCardSim, then the bridge
mvn -B test
mvn -B package -DskipTests
java -jar bridge/target/bridge.jar --port 9876

# the host code against a federation in the test process
cd host && cargo test --workspace

The bridge takes POST /apdu with {"apdu":"hex"} and answers the response data and status word. Set CARD_BACKEND=soft, bridge or pcsc to choose what the host code talks to.

Installing on a card

Build the CAP file with Ant and the Java Card 3.0.5 SDK, then install it with GlobalPlatformPro on a blank J3R180 with its default keys:

cd applet && ant cap -Djc.sdk=$HOME/.javacard/sdks/jc305u4_kit
gp --install target/fedimint-card-0.1.cap --applet F0464D434152444D
gp --create F0464D4341524401 --package F0464D43415244 --applet F0464D4341524401
  • Each failed attempt with wrong keys counts toward locking the card for good, so don't retry gp on a card whose keys you don't know.
  • On an ACR122U reader, --bs 64 loads reliably.
  • For issuing cards, the provisioner app installs from a phone and replaces the default keys with per-card ones.

The CAP build guide has the pinned SDK, the checks and the findings from silicon.

Known limits

  • 8 slots, so a card holds at most 8 notes. A 16-slot build failed to install on the J3R180. Cards with 32 slots are in development.
  • No command reports the card's state, no PIN unblock, and no way for the owner to sign a PIN change.
  • The applet is meant for contactless use. Some commands may stall on a T=0 contact reader.
  • Every payment needs the till, the registry and the federation online.

Issues and security

Report a bug, or a place where these docs and the code disagree, as a GitHub issue. Report anything that could affect funds privately, through a security advisory or to hi@fedimintcard.org, as the security policy asks.
